title: UX storyboards: illustrative recovery guides for throttles, latency expiries, and resend strategies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a set of onboarding/quickstart UX assets and doc graphics that clearly show users how to recover when calls fail due to rate limiting (429), request timeouts, and transient network errors requiring retries. Deliverables should be usable in the Console docs, the quickstart walkthrough, and the SDK README.

Deliverables:
1) Three storyboard sequences (thumbnail + 3 panels each) that illustrate: a) soft throttle (user-friendly 429 explanation + cool-down suggestion), b) long-tail latency expiry (what to check and when to retry), c) best-effort resend flow (client backoff + idempotency hint).
2) Two micro-animation prototypes demonstrating exponential backoff visual feedback and a retry countdown. Provide Lottie-compatible exports.
3) Annotated screenshot overlays for the Console error panel (desktop + mobile breakpoints) showing where to find request IDs, retry buttons, and links to logs/trace.
4) One-page SDK integrator cheat sheet graphic (PNG + SVG) showing sample code snippets, recommended retry/backoff policy, and mapping of server codes to suggested actions.
5) Figma component library update: new callout token, error icon set, stepper component for storyboards, and localization-ready text layers.

Design constraints: Support light/dark themes, WCAG AA contrast, and easily translatable copy. Tone: concise, action-oriented, and non-blaming (assume system rather than user at fault). Align copy with Console SLO messaging and runtime fallback language.

Acceptance criteria:
- PM and Eng sign-off on hi-fi Figma file.
- Assets exported to docs-assets bucket (SVG/PNG/Lottie) with naming convention and metadata.
- Console quickstart page updated with new annotated screenshots and cheat sheet.
- A short integration example added to SDK README and linked from docs.
- PR created for docs update and assigned to docs owner.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Kickoff: scoped deliverables with PM (Arjun Patel) and Eng lead (Sofia Ramires). Agreed to include both animation and static fallback images for bandwidth-sensitive customers.

2026-03-11 — Low-fi sketches uploaded to Figma; included three storyboard directions (empathetic, diagnostic, procedural). Luca prefers the procedural direction for developer audiences; Maya suggests keeping one empathetic variant for onboarding emails.

2026-03-12 — PM feedback: ensure cheat sheet includes exact SDK snippet for retry-with-jitter and link to runtime docs. Eng requested an extra panel showing network-edge partial success (some tokens accepted, others failed) and guidance to surface partial-response info in Console.

2026-03-12 — Design decision: use shared callout color token (error-callout-500) and a neutral animated spinner for retry, avoid attention-grabbing red to reduce alarm. Added accessibility checklist to Figma file.
2026-03-12 — Next steps: produce hi-fi storyboards and micro-animations by 2026-03-20, then schedule review with PM and Eng the week of 2026-03-22. Prepare assets export checklist for docs engineers.
notes: Avoid duplicating existing 'troubleshoot cards' art; goal is more stepwise recovery guidance that developers can map to code examples. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to capture customer-observed failure narratives (SRE ticket summaries).
acceptance_test_steps: 1) Open Figma hi-fi and verify all panels match copy and tokens. 2) Export assets and confirm file sizes and formats (SVG for icons, PNG 2x for screenshots, Lottie for animations). 3) Update docs PR with new assets and sample SDK snippet; link to CI docs build. 4) Get PM + Eng approval on PR.
